# Deployment Targets and Credentials

## Start Here

[Target model](../../../src/desktop/deployment.rs), [credential store](../../../src/desktop/deployment/credentials.rs), [named tokens](../../../src/desktop/deployment/tokens.rs), and [desktop deployment UI](../../../src/desktop/ui).

## Procedure and Invariants

1. Keep public target settings separate from secrets. Direct-entry credentials remain scoped to canonical workspace/landing identity and target ID. Explicit named tokens use a separate per-user `named:<uuid>` keyring namespace; never implicitly share a direct-entry credential.
1. Use the OS credential abstraction and zeroizing secret buffers. Never serialize tokens into target files, run snapshots, progress events, logs, or diagnostic text.
1. Preserve existing credentials when an edit does not replace them. Make target save/provider-switch/delete failure paths explicit; do not leave a saved target referencing a removed secret or silently lose a previously usable credential.
1. Validate target/provider/suite selection again at execution. Missing credentials or unavailable secure storage must produce actionable secret-free errors.
1. Settings read, directory-creation, and save failures must identify the local operation/path and retain the underlying OS error. Preserve existing bytes on failure; never clear read-only attributes or change permissions automatically. Cover Windows error 5 and blocked settings directories in the existing model tests.
1. Cloudflare uses `provider: cloudflareWorkers` with a `cloudflare` object containing `accountId`, `workerName`, and saved routing/asset options; never repurpose Azure `environment` or Netlify `siteId`. Omitted `workersDev` defaults to public production (`true`); explicit `null` preserves routing. Keep this object absent for other providers and retain advanced options on ordinary edits.
1. Keep production Windows credential persistence semantics separate from the mock backend used in tests. Do not validate against the user's actual keyring.
1. Named tokens support Netlify and Cloudflare, with immutable provider/account identity and editable name/secret. Serialize only metadata and `namedTokenId` references. Revalidate provider/account when linking and executing; deleting a target must never remove a named token.
1. Catalog writes lock and compare the loaded catalog, rejecting stale windows. Preserve secrets on failed metadata saves and clear masked drafts on cancel/close. Named-token removal must warn that referencing targets will require another token.
1. Landing targets use app-managed identity, not linked-site workspaces. See the [landing skill](../desktop-landing-apps/SKILL.md).
1. Store the optional `publishedUrl` with its target ID after successful publication. Reload current settings before updating, preserve other targets/selection, and reject removed or changed destinations. Accept only credential-free HTTPS URLs without query/fragment data. Failure/cancellation retains the previous URL.
1. Name-only edits, Cloudflare asset options, and Netlify/Cloudflare token changes preserve the URL. Destination/routing-mode changes clear it; replacing an Azure token also clears it because the token identifies the app. A confirmed private Cloudflare publication clears stale URLs; failure/cancellation does not. Surface persistence errors without hiding a successful URL. Report completion writes in the runner's background task; landing completion writes before returning to the UI.
1. `reportPublications` stores target IDs and suite output IDs in completion order, atomically with report URLs. Replace membership when redeploying that target/site, clear it with invalidated URLs or removed targets, and retain it on failure/cancellation. Resolve the latest publication containing every requested suite; single suites use URL path-segment encoding under `/suites/`. Legacy URLs without membership must not imply that a suite was published. Load Runs links off the UI thread and refresh after completion or target changes.
1. Report deployments are `DeploymentJob.mode` Update (keep other suites, optional `removeIds`) or Replace (site = selection; saved requests default to Replace). Updates may not empty a site.
   - [Site state](../../../src/desktop/deployment/site_state.rs) `/_snapshot/deployment.json` is published with the site and is untrusted when read back: validate decoded paths with snapshot segment rules and report URLs through `versioned_path`, since suite IDs may need percent-encoding.
   - [Incremental planning](../../../src/desktop/deployment/incremental.rs) prefers the site's state, then the destination-bound local copy (`<settings>.sites/<target>.json`, forgotten on destination change or target removal, kept through uploads), and refuses blind updates of previously published sites (`site_state::published_before`, which the suite list also applies so such a site never shows as empty; a `<target>.published` marker covers private Cloudflare publications without URL or membership; a previously published site that now reads as empty counts as unreadable). The local copy is forgotten before uploads that remove suites, and only on real destination changes (post-commit failures warn).
   - Netlify and Cloudflare keep files by provider hash (`KeptFiles`) and fail before upload when the provider lacks kept content. A kept file the staged site also holds (a capture-log chunk shared with a regenerated suite) is listed and budgeted once, and differing content fails. Legacy sites regenerate kept suites from local results. Cloudflare budget retries are dormant in production (`content_budget()` is `None` outside tests; see the [Cloudflare skill](../deployment-cloudflare/SKILL.md)). With a budget, `KeptSuitesOverBudget` makes `ReportDeployment::generate_and_publish` retry through `retry_with_kept_suites`, whose doc comment is the authoritative description of the steps. Keep its invariants: kept suites are never read or rewritten (`image_roles`, `refresh_site_versions`, and `optimized_state` skip them, and `optimized_state` records `SuiteState.source_bytes` for each suite it shrinks); each retry brings back at least one kept suite (`Plan::upload_kept_suites`) or sets `Prepared.budget.reduce_quality` (`BudgetRetry`) once, so the loop ends with every suite local at the latest; quality stays at or above `SPREAD_QUALITY` while suites stay kept. The retry's second `application::execute` reuses the worker process's settings (same workspace only), and its failure is reported with Replace advice.
   - Azure updates re-upload kept suites and unchanged selected ones from the report output (`Plan::reuse_local`, `Plan.local`). Each attempt of `ReportDeployment::generate_and_publish` (`generate_and_publish_once`) runs `stash_local` before generation, which prunes unselected suites from the output: every file must match the state's size and provider hash, or the suite is regenerated (`Plan::regenerate_local`). Reads and writes use the staging symlink rules (`artifact_source`, `restore_file`). `publish` stages the stash with the generated suites (generated copies of shared files win and are recorded), refuses an unchecked plan, and on every exit restores reused suites into the output (warning only): the whole staged site once staging completed, otherwise the stashed files; the attempt does the same when generation fails (`restore_after_failure`). Azure Update needs no local results for kept suites until their copies fail verification.
   - Optimized Cloudflare uploads rewrite the state (`Manifest::rewrite_optimized_state`: refreshed summaries, optimized hashes) in the upload and in staging, and the deployment records the staged copy it reads back; only a state that cannot be rewritten or is excluded is dropped (`state_dropped`), which forgets the local copy.
   - Per-suite skip (`Plan::keep_unchanged`, Update only, Netlify/Cloudflare, known compatible state, unforced) keeps a selected suite whose record in `<target>.inputs.json` still matches: `SuiteInputs::matches` compares `suite_input_fingerprint` (report text omitted) and the `suite_digest` of the site's `SuiteState`. Replace rebuilds every selected suite, which is why kept-content errors advise it.
   - Records exist for every provider, name the state the site serves (content-only skips record against the served state, never the staged one), are never published, need no write-ahead because a stale one cannot match, are ignored when corrupt, and are removed by `forget_target`.
   - The suite list and dialog apply the same rule through `SuiteInputs::verify` (`SiteSuites.verified`, recomputed off the UI thread after site reads and artifact scans): a digest mismatch counts as changed; suites without a record or local output fall back to run IDs. Previews rebuild unchanged suites for Replace and count changes for every provider.
1. Each publication's optional `siteFingerprint` is `deployment_fingerprint`: the staged site (generation timestamps excluded) plus provider, environment, site, and Cloudflare settings, never names, URLs, or credentials. Before generating reports, the worker computes `deployment_input_fingerprint` (suite-output file paths, sizes, and mtimes, without `.lock`/`.tmp` files or dot temp directories, plus report text, build, and site settings). A match with the publication's `inputFingerprint` emits an unchanged result and skips snapshot, staging, and upload. Inputs that cannot be fingerprinted only disable this early check. After staging, the worker reads current settings from `WorkerRequest.deploymentSettings`. It refuses a job whose target was removed or whose publication settings changed (only name and URL may differ), because Deploy anyway replays a saved request. It skips the upload only for an unforced job whose fingerprint matches. Otherwise it clears the fingerprint *before* uploading (write-ahead), so a crash cannot leave a stale match; landing uploads do the same. A content-only skip records the new inputs with `record_report_inputs` and otherwise changes nothing. `site_fingerprint` trusts the verification `stage_reports` already did and reads only unversioned files. Failed, cancelled, or result-less runs also clear the fingerprint and keep membership. Deploy anyway sets `DeploymentJob.force` and goes back through the normal run guard. Unreadable settings fail before upload.
1. Deployment and named-token edit forms use toolkit Form/Field for labels only. Keep stable input IDs and accessible names, provider-dependent controls, masked password content types, saved-secret placeholders, and the existing save/cancel locks and draft clearing behavior.
1. Saved target/token Select items use stable IDs separate from names; provider items use machine keys. Reconcile rejected confirmations to the authoritative selection. Confirming an unchanged token source or provider preserves the secret draft; actual identity changes clear it. Keep missing selected identities visible and non-deployable.

## Checks

```sh
cargo test --features desktop --lib desktop::deployment::credentials::tests
cargo test --features desktop --lib desktop::deployment::tests
cargo test --features desktop --lib desktop::deployment::tokens::tests
cargo test --features desktop --lib completed_deployments_persist_urls
cargo test --features desktop --lib published_report_sites_
cargo test --features desktop --lib -- report_fingerprints_ unchanged_deployments_ deployment_fingerprints_ skipped_deployments_ input_fingerprints_ early_checks_
cargo test --features desktop --lib -- site_state incremental preview merged_staging kept_ unchanged_selected_ suite_input_records_ selected_suites_with_unchanged_ verification_matches_ suite_input_fingerprints_ optimized_uploads_publish_ whole_site_ budget_ lossless_estimates_ quality_reductions_spread_ suites_reduced_before_ spreading_retries_size_
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib suite_statuses_follow_recorded_inputs
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib deploy_dialog_summarizes
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib skipped_deployment_
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib saved_deployment_urls_reopen_and_copy
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib runs_open_site_
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib desktop::ui::tokens::tests
cargo test --features gui-tests --lib desktop::ui::deployment::tests
```

Cover workspace isolation, create/edit/delete, blank/missing tokens, provider changes, failed saves, corrupt target files, and errors that omit synthetic secrets. Run `./ci/desktop-smoke.ps1 -PublishingFlows` for named-token and landing controls; run the smoke harness self-tests first and preserve the interactive-desktop guards.

## Maintain

Update [desktop docs](../../../docs/desktop.md) and this skill when storage or target workflow changes. Comment credential ownership and rollback decisions.
